cells: Hayman–Lingham Problem 7.73 (W. H. J. Fuchs), problem 2307073: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.07200v2#page=184 (printed p. 183)

Yixin He and Quanyu Tang, On Fuchs's additive intersection problem for the hyperbolic metric, arXiv:2603.16676v1 (17 March 2026), Theorem 1.2 and §3: the full original arbitrary-domain question has a negative answer. For every fixed R>0, no finite A(R) bounds the intersection hyperbolic density by A(R) times the sum of the two individual densities. Symmetric one-punctured disks give a quotient tending to infinity. This is a credited verification/rederivation of the existing preprint, with no novelty or first-resolution claim. The original v2 problem and He–Tang v1 PDF bodies were freshly retrieved, authenticated and inspected; the general-domain proof and its essential covering, monotonicity, punctured-disk and scaling inputs were checked. Acceptance is limited to this general-domain result; the simply connected bound, its endpoint, lower extremals and capacity arguments are not audited here. The DOI identifies an arXiv preprint; journal publication and peer-review status were not verified. This internal audit is AI-assisted, with no external human review or proof-assistant certification.
